issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Institutional Failure: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, 'institutional failure' and especially 'betrayal by someone trusted' are hard to reconcile unless the crash involved unusual interpersonal circumstances not reflected anywhere else in the profile. The rest of the profile centers on fear/startle/intrusive sensory recall, which fits an accident trauma; these appraisal items instead imply an interpersonal or systemic-trauma narrative.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: 'Guilt on recall' can occur after accidents, but in this profile it sits awkwardly with the chosen appraisal set: the appraisals focus on betrayal/institutional failure rather than self-blame or responsibility. That makes the guilt theme insufficiently supported across nodes for a coherent cognitive formulation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, the appraisal 'I was betrayed by someone I trusted' is hard to reconcile unless the crash specifically involved a trusted driver or intentional wrongdoing, which is not otherwise reflected anywhere else in the profile. As presented, it introduces a different interpersonal-trauma theme that is not supported by the rest of the selected items.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted
issues.explanation: Within Negative Appraisals, 'Betrayal' and 'Self-Blame' can sometimes coexist, but in this profile they point to different causal narratives for the trauma (trusted other's betrayal vs one's own actions causing the event) without any supporting context. That makes the appraisal set clinically hard to unify around a single MVC trauma narrative.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Other-Blame Rumination: I dwell on what other people have done to me
issues.explanation: The profile contains a hard-to-reconcile blame pattern: strong self-blame and guilt are paired with other-blame rumination as a core maladaptive strategy. Mixed blame can occur, but this combination is the main internal inconsistency in the selected items because the appraisals and memory items point toward inward blame, while the strategy item points toward sustained outward blame.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted
issues.explanation: Within the cognitive formulation, Maladaptive Strategies links most strongly to Negative Appraisals, so the strategy content should fit the appraisal style. Here the appraisal style is dominated by self-blame, helplessness, and permanent emotional damage, making other-blame rumination the least coherent strategy item.

issues.item: Memory: Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, guilt on recall is plausible, especially with self-blame, so it is not problematic by itself. The concern is specifically its combination with persistent other-blame rumination, which pulls the profile toward a different blame direction than the rest of the formulation.

vignette: José, a 62-year-old Latin American man, has been a dancer his entire life. His passion for dance brought him joy and purpose until a life-threatening motor vehicle collision six months ago. The accident occurred during one of his performances in the city, when an out-of-control car veered onto the stage, sending shards of glass and debris flying everywhere. José was grazed by broken pieces of the stage lighting, leaving deep cuts across his arms and face. In that moment, he felt a profound sense of helplessness as he watched the chaos unfold around him. Since the accident, José has been navigating through life with a new set of fears and anxieties. He had come to believe that he will never be able to feel normal emotions again, and that the event happened to him because of who he is. The trauma has left deep emotional scars, making it difficult for him to experience the joy and passion he once felt for dance. José has developed several maladaptive strategies to cope with his distress. He often deliberately tries to leave his body or blank out whenever thoughts of the accident start creeping in. This dissociation helps him escape from the intense negative feelings that arise when he thinks about what happened. He also stays up until very late, delaying sleep as a way to avoid nightmares and intrusive memories. When he does try to sleep, he is plagued by vivid auditory recollections of the sounds he heard during the accident-the screeching tires, shattering glass, and panicked shouts. Despite his best efforts to suppress thoughts about the trauma, José often finds himself scanning for exits as soon as he enters any room or building. This hyper-vigilance makes him feel more in control and less vulnerable, but it has also led to significant avoidance behaviors. He avoids performances and rehearsals at all costs, fearing that another accident could happen again. As a result, his dance career has suffered significantly. José's marriage has also been strained by his trauma symptoms. His wife notices how much he withdraws from social activities they used to enjoy together. When she touches him unexpectedly, José reacts with alarm and often pulls away. This physical touch sensitivity has created tension in their relationship, as his wife struggles to understand why her attempts at closeness are met with such resistance. The most debilitating aspect of the trauma for José is the intense shame he feels when recalling the event. He can't seem to put the frightening experience into words and often remains silent about it, even though his family and friends have offered support. The shame compounds his feelings of helplessness and character blame, leading him to believe that the accident was a direct result of his perceived shortcomings. What frightened José most was the realization that despite all his training and expertise as a dancer, he couldn't prevent the accident from happening. He felt utterly helpless and began to lose faith in his own abilities and worth. These negative appraisals have made it difficult for him to re-engage with dance or even leave his home. José finally sought help because he recognized that his life was becoming increasingly isolated and unfulfilled. His wife encouraged him to seek professional support, emphasizing that he didn't need to face these challenges alone. José is most hoping for a way to reconnect with the joy and passion he once felt for dance while learning how to manage his intense fears and intrusive memories. Through therapy, José hopes to regain control over his life and rebuild his sense of self without the constant burden of fear and shame. He wants to rediscover the dancer within him and find a path forward that feels safe and meaningful again.
